content: You help people edit Power BI paginated reports (.rdl files) using the pbirb tools. Tools are available for data sources, datasets and queries, parameters, tables and matrices, text and cell styling, page layout, headers and footers, charts, images, and actions. The user's message names the report file. Make the requested change directly without asking for confirmation, and keep the rest of the report intact. If the tools cannot do what is asked, say so plainly instead of improvising.

Report file: /var/folders/zl/zqyf2h6n3md3dcg8g9cdfm380000gp/T/pbirb-eval-q03-27_sw67n/report.rdl

Report Builder refuses to open this report. What's wrong with it? Don't change anything yet.

{"valid": false, "errors": [{"severity": "error", "rule": "xsd", "location": "/var/folders/zl/zqyf2h6n3md3dcg8g9cdfm380000gp/T/pbirb-eval-q03-27_sw67n/report.rdl:87", "message": "Element '{http://schemas.microsoft.com/sqlserver/reporting/2016/01/reportdefinition}Action': This element is not expected."}], "xsd_used": true}
Let me look at the element around line 87.

The report fails schema validation at one spot, and that is almost certainly why Report Builder won't open it. I haven't changed anything.

**The problem:** The `HeaderProductID` textbox in `MainTable` (around line 87) has a bare `<Action>` element as a direct child:

```xml
<Style/>
<Action><Hyperlink>="https://example.com"</Hyperlink></Action>
</Textbox>
```

The RDL schema doesn't allow `<Action>` there. Actions have to be wrapped in an `<ActionInfo><Actions>...</Actions></ActionInfo>` block, and that block has to sit where the schema expects it in the textbox. The validator reports exactly one error:

> Element 'Action': This element is not expected.

**What I'd do to fix it (not yet applied):** Replace the bare `<Action>` with a correctly wrapped `<ActionInfo>` block containing the same hyperlink. The hyperlink expression itself (`="https://example.com"`) looks valid, so it can stay as is. After the fix I'd re-run validation to confirm the report passes.

Everything else I checked looks fine: the data source, the dataset, the two parameters (`DateFrom`, `DateTo`), and the table layout are all present, and no other schema errors were reported. Say the word and I'll apply the fix.
